about: Written by hand: how each program assembles the server from the shared crates, as an ordered flow (steps), and which implementation the program passes to which slots (wiring): one entry per implementation and crate, naming every function it goes to. An implementation is a public item (crate::path), or, for a type of the program's own that is not public, a description (own). generate.py stops if a step names an item that is gone, or a wiring names an item or a slot that is not there. A program with "inferred": false shows only its hand-written wiring: for kkt, pairing by names gives wrong pairs. "injectors" lists the wiring that a shared crate does itself (kkt-server, which assembles the server), in the same form; an entry that passes on what it was given names it in "own" and its supplier in "supplier".

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Flags, the config file (found from the machine's facts, which kkt-machine-os reads; read through kkt-config-file-os and parsed by kkt-config-file) and defaults, such as kkt-setup's default database, become each owner's settings: ServeOptions layers the flags over the file, and its resolve fills the rest from the owners' defaults, mapping the keys kkt-server builds with onto ServerSettings (server_settings); the key files are checked, which gives the admission of /mcp, the web page and /mcp-admin.

steps.title: Database
steps.text: A SqlitePlace for the database file, adopting a database from before kkt-db as kkt-rules' history describes it in kkt-db's Legacy shape, with the program's too-old message, opens it with the core's tables; the kkt-db Backend its open gives is the store's database.

steps.title: Run record
steps.text: The owners word their settings and the program supplies its own plain record lines; ServerSettings orders them. The program maps the run into NewServerRun, and kkt-rules start records it and builds the Rules.

steps.title: Parts
steps.text: The Rules start built, the system clock and the operating system's randomness they were built with, and key mode's identity go into the server's parts. Parts takes the API as Arc<dyn AdminApi>, the checked settings snapshot.
steps.fills: kkt-server::Parts::new (rules, clock, entropy, identify, log, checked)

steps.title: Config
steps.text: The three admissions and optional instructions text go into AppConfig; component settings and the checked hosts go through Parts.

steps.title: Build and run
steps.text: build assembles the server from the parts and config; listen binds it; serve_until answers until a stop signal, and the program logs a socket option it could not set.

also.title: The agents' commands
also.text: kkt register, reclaim, watch and connect run in kkt-agent-commands over AgentParts, which main.rs builds once, beside the operator's parts, with agent_parts from the implementations it chooses: kkt-setup's connection question answered from this machine's setup record and serve settings (ConnectionReads), kkt-agent-client's Mcp, injected as it is as its Servers, kkt-agent-files-os' credential and state files under kkt-setup's credential-file rule, the key files, kkt's path, the terminal and the system clock.

also.title: The operator's commands
also.text: main.rs builds the operator's parts once, a NativeOperate with the service capability (ServeArgs), and gives every operator command its OperateParts: native containers, services, client files, probes, lane disk, clock, setup and key files, database, backups and terminal. ServeReads answers config, database, key and installed-service questions only when asked; ConnectionReads supplies the shared connection selection. Commands that can inspect an unrecorded service require ServiceDefaults, which only parts built with ServeArgs have. CLI parsing and serving remain in the program. Service planning reads the program's service inputs and retains its opaque source context in a deferred CheckService, called only after the plan succeeds. The native try_bind callback checks the address before installation. Setup and switch compose their steps in operate, reading PATH once when detecting clients, staging keys and updating config text through supplied providers. TerminalLines asks the questions and TerminalLink supplies Docker login. Before kkt serve, check_setup reads the record through the same parts.
